description: c118/c3813 connectivity-pillar peer-link smoke. Two PerfectDark.exe processes in one install dir: a listen-host (--host + --listen-bind 27200, writes pd-host.log via the natural --host log routing) and a client (--connect-host 127.0.0.1:27200, writes pd-client.log). The runner launches the host first, polls pd-host.log for the 'NET: created server on port 27200' barrier, then launches the client. Both processes share the same --smoke JSON path so they execute the same scripted exit at t=90000ms; the long budget is intentional because a clean shared install can spend tens of seconds validating or extracting typed archives before the listen-bind fast path fires. Assertions run against the concatenation of both logs. Sister to listen_host_init_smoke, which only proves the ENet stack BINDS -- this test proves a two-process ENet peer connection actually round-trips. Adds c118 fast-paths --listen-bind <port> and --connect-host <addr>:<port> in port/src/main.c that fire netStartServer / netStartClient on the first mainTick where g_NetInit is true. NOTE: when the orchestrated host receives an actual ENet client connection on loopback, the host's mainTick path can fail to take the scripted exit cleanly. The runner's per-process WaitForExit + watchdog handles this -- the host is reaped after timeout_seconds and the client's clean exit sentinel proves the peer link succeeded. The SMOKE: result=scripted_exit count is therefore min: 1 (client only), not 2 -- the test passes when the client sees the host's bind, completes CLC_AUTH, and exits cleanly.

input_sequence.comment: Both processes share this schedule. The host arms --listen-bind in bootApplyCliFastPaths and fires netStartServer on the first mainTick frame where g_NetInit is true; the client arms --connect-host the same way and fires netStartClient. The runner's wait_for barrier waits for the host's 'NET: created server on port 27200' log line before launching the client, so the client's enet_host_connect target is already up. ENet's connect-handshake roundtrip is sub-100ms on loopback; the client's CLSTATE_AUTH transition lands within the first second after netStartClient.

Scripted exit at 90s. On a warm install the peer link is established within a few seconds; on a clean install the typed-archive validation/extraction pass can run before --listen-bind fires, so this fixture must leave enough budget for extraction plus the host/client handshake. The client emits SMOKE: result=scripted_exit at client-t=90s. If the host's harness exit does not fire after the peer connection, the runner's watchdog kills the host after the watchdog timeout, which is fine -- by then the assertions have already matched on the host bind, incoming connection, CLC_AUTH, and client clean exit.

required_lines: NET: connected to server, sending CLC_AUTH
NET: client slot \d+ assigned to peer
forbidden_patterns: NET: could not init ENet, disabling networking
NET: could not create ENet host on port \d+

required_counts.pattern: NET: connected to server, sending CLC_AUTH
